content: The test image shows a soybean trifoliate leaf with scattered small yellow-green spots/lesions on the upper surface. Comparing the three candidates:
- **Downy mildew**: Bottom-left panel shows pale yellow-white scattered spots on upper leaf surface — very close match to test image
- **Bacterial Blight**: Shows more angular, water-soaked to brown lesions — less matching
- **Soybean Vein necrosis virus**: Top-right shows hand-held leaf with scattered yellow spots — also similar

The test image shows small, pale chlorotic spots scattered across the upper leaf surface without necrotic brown centers. This most closely matches **Downy mildew**, where pale yellow spots appear on the upper leaf surface (with grayish sporulation typically on the underside). The scatter pattern and pale yellow-green coloration are characteristic.
